html:
The Atfalati, or Tualatin, are a Kalapuya people of north-western Oregon, whose villages stood on the Tualatin Plains, around Wapato Lake and in the hills west of today's Portland. They spoke the northern dialect of the Kalapuyan language.

They gathered camas bulbs and wapato roots, hunted deer and elk, and burned the valley floor to keep it open as prairie. In the early 1830s an epidemic of malaria, the "fever and ague", swept the lower Columbia and Willamette Valley and killed most of the Kalapuya. Settlers coming over the Oregon Trail took the rest of the valley. In 1855 the survivors signed a treaty and were moved to the Grand Ronde Reservation, where their descendants belong to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde.
